items.headline: Carhartt WIP × Nike are back with a boot
items.caption: Their first sneaker collab in eight years: the Air Max Goadome Low.
body: It comes in 'Twilight Marsh', 'Black' and a third colourway.
It looks more sneaker than boot.
How to wear it: double-knee work pants and a chore coat.

items.headline: Converse made Chuck Taylors for chefs
items.caption: 'At Your Service' Chucks have non-slip soles and water-repellent canvas.
body: The workplace line adds CX cushioning for long shifts.
From courts to streets to kitchens.
How to wear it: with an apron, or with jeans off-shift.

items.headline: Graphpaper × Descente: tech gear without the cosplay
items.caption: Weather-ready staples that don't look like hiking kit.
body: The Japanese labels give everyday pieces a technical upgrade.
It's performance wear without the tactical look.
How to wear it: a clean shell over tailored trousers.

items.headline: Runners in suits and Oxfords at the NYC Marathon
items.caption: Santoni's 295g Easy Run Oxford, tested at 26.2 miles.
body: Three racers ran in suits, ties and the new shoes.
They weigh about as much as a running shoe.
How to wear it: to the office, not the marathon.

items.headline: Slim trousers are back, say the CFDA red carpets
items.caption: Men at the US fashion awards swapped wide legs for slimmer cuts.
body: Blazers and ties were expected; the slim trousers weren't.
GQ asks if it's a real comeback.
How to wear it: slim, not skinny, with a cropped hem.

items.headline: Style lessons from JFK Jr.
items.caption: A writer who studied his wardrobe for a book shares five lessons.
body: He biked in suits and wore waistcoats with jeans.
He didn't invent these looks, he just did them better.
How to wear it: a navy suit, worn like casual clothes.

items.headline: Jude Bellingham fronts Calvin Klein underwear
items.caption: The Real Madrid star joins CK's long line of athlete models.
body: Oliver Hadlee Pearch shot the campaign on a hot Madrid day.
A teaser clip drove Instagram wild first.
Style lesson: good basics are the foundation.

items.headline: Pierce Brosnan dresses like landed gentry in 'MobLand'
items.caption: His gangster dresses to blend in, not to stand out.
body: Conrad Harrigan's look is quiet country tailoring.
Esquire shows how to steal it.
How to wear it: tweed jacket, knit tie, brogues.

items.headline: Adam Brody, The Rake's cover star
items.caption: From 'The O.C.' to 'Nobody Wants This', a new kind of leading man.
body: Brody talks about fame, what he lost and why this time is different.
He's the cover of The Rake's Issue 108.
Style lesson: grown-up tailoring, worn easy.

items.headline: Beavers return to Loch Ness after 500 years
items.caption: Scotland approves bringing the 'ecosystem engineers' back.
body: Beavers were last seen around Loch Ness in 1526–27.
NatureScot granted a licence on 30 October to release a pair.
They help create wetlands that support other wildlife.

items.headline: A rare-blood donor gives at all 85 Australian blood banks
items.caption: Trevor Bergman has donated 545 times.
body: He's one of about 150 Australians with the anti-D antibody.
Anti-D helps protect babies of pregnant mothers.
The 59-year-old police officer finished his tour of every donation centre.

items.headline: A wheelchair athlete now teaches wheelchair skateboarding
items.caption: Xie Junwu climbed mountains and ran marathons. Now he coaches.
body: He runs what is likely China's first wheelchair skateboarding training centre.
He helps others build confidence moving in their chairs.
Barriers, broken.
